content:
Geometry in Class 4 spans lines, angles, circles, solids and symmetry — visual questions where knowing the exact facts wins. This guide covers what the IMO Class 4 geometry chapter tests, the facts to know cold, and a free 10-question test.

What the Class 4 Maths Olympiad Geometry chapter tests

  • Lines, rays, segments; parallel and perpendicular lines
  • Angle types (acute, right, obtuse, straight)
  • Circles — radius, diameter and d = 2r
  • Solids (cube/cuboid facts) and lines of symmetry

Key facts your child should know

  • Acute < 90°; right = 90°; obtuse between 90° and 180°; straight = 180°.
  • Diameter = 2 × radius; radius = diameter ÷ 2.
  • A cube/cuboid has 6 faces, 12 edges, 8 vertices; opposite dice faces total 7.
  • Lines of symmetry: square 4, rectangle 2, equilateral triangle 3, circle unlimited.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Mixing up radius and diameter.
  • Counting edges as vertices on a solid.
  • Assuming every triangle has a line of symmetry (a scalene has none).

quiz.title: IMO Class 4 Geometry Quiz
quiz.intro: Ten Olympiad-pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: How many lines of symmetry does the capital letter Z have?
questions.explanation: The capital letter Z has 0 lines of symmetry.

questions.q: Which of these regular shapes CANNOT tile a floor all by itself without gaps?
questions.explanation: The angles of a regular pentagon (108°) cannot add up to 360° around a point, so gaps are always left; the other three tessellate.

questions.q: How many lines of symmetry does the capital letter O have?
questions.explanation: The capital letter O has many (unlimited) lines of symmetry.

questions.q: Two lines that never meet, however far they are extended, are called
questions.explanation: Lines keeping the same distance apart and never meeting are parallel.

questions.q: All the radii of one circle are
questions.explanation: Every radius of a circle has the same length.

questions.q: How many diameters can be drawn in one circle?
questions.explanation: A diameter can be drawn through the centre in any direction — endlessly many.

questions.q: Two angles together make one right angle. If one of them is 35°, what is the other?
questions.explanation: A right angle is 90°, so the other angle is 90 - 35 = 55°.

questions.q: The rungs (steps) of a straight ladder are an example of
questions.explanation: The rungs of a ladder stay the same distance apart and never meet — they are parallel.

questions.q: An angle measures 89°. What type of angle is it?
questions.explanation: 89° is less than 90°, so it is an acute angle.

questions.q: The capital letter T shows mainly which pair of lines?
questions.explanation: In T, the top stroke meets the vertical stroke at 90° — perpendicular.

faq.q: What is the difference between radius and diameter?
faq.a: The radius runs from the centre to the circle; the diameter crosses the whole circle through the centre and equals two radii.
